rules.problem: Mixes the red-box urgent signs with non-urgent impaction risk factors (bed-bound, palliative care, overflow diarrhoea) that come from the 'not needing urgent attention' section and are already in the impaction check task.

rules.rule: Check for faecal impaction in constipation
rules.problem: Trigger omits the page's '> 65 years' criterion (the grammar has no numeric age; should be recorded as a known limitation). Otherwise faithful.

rules.rule: Check for colorectal cancer symptoms in constipation
rules.problem: Drops 'change in bowel habits / stool consistency' (only Diarrhea), drops 'persistent' on abdominal discomfort/cramps/gas, omits Abdominal pain that the diagnosis rule uses, and does not check the page's risk factors (previous CRC/polyps/UC/Crohn's, first-degree family history, Lynch).

rules.rule: Diagnose probable faecal impaction in constipation
rules.problem: Structure and 'probable' are faithful to 'If present, impaction likely'; '> 65 years' branch missing (grammar limit) and 'Fecal impaction of rectum' is the closer concept.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible colorectal cancer in constipation
rules.problem: Page has no 'consider/suspect colorectal cancer' wording, only 'discuss/refer'. The rule labels possible colorectal cancer for constipation plus any single non-specific symptom (fatigue, gas, weakness, transient abdominal pain), ignoring 'persistent' and the >50-years/history risk criteria, so it will fire for a large share of constipation patients.

rules.rule: Urgent: constipation with no stools or flatus for 24 hours
rules.problem: Urgent is justified by 'Give urgent attention ... Refer same day'. AND of no-stool and no-flatus for >=24 h (onset at least 24 h ago, per house convention) plus pain OR distension matches 'No stools or flatus/wind in the past 24 hours with abdominal pain/distension'.

summary: Most consequential: the possible colorectal cancer diagnosis is not stated on the page (it says only 'discuss/refer') and fires on constipation plus any one non-specific symptom, dropping 'persistent' and ignoring the >50-years/history risk criteria. Impaction risk factors (bed-bound, palliative care, overflow diarrhoea) are misplaced in the urgent check task, and the colorectal check misses altered bowel habit/stool consistency. The red-box priority rule is faithful; also note the page's 'anaemia likely' (Hb <12 woman / <13 man) is not encoded anywhere.
